The NUMA code is smart enough to distribute the memory of workloads
that span multiple NUMA nodes across those NUMA nodes.
However
column2: it still has a pretty high scan rate for such workloads

column1: because any memory that is left on a node other than the node of
the CPU that faulted on the memory is counted as non-local
causes the scan rate to go up.
Counting the memory on any node where the task's numa group is
actively running as local
column2: allows the scan rate to slow down

column1: once the application is settled in.
This should reduce the overhead of the automatic NUMA placement
code
column2: when a workload spans multiple NUMA nodes.
